paragraphs: If you are willing to complete methane testing, ventilation and roof support checks before starting the machine, and to take responsibility for the safety conditions of your shift mates, this occupation is worth learning more about; people who find checks troublesome and want to start the machine straight away rarely last.

If you can accept 100% daily exposure to dust and contaminants at the work face, 96% daily in intrusive noise and 93% daily near hazardous equipment, with 92% of the time not in a climate-controlled indoor setting, this job will use that tolerance every day; people who only want to work in a well-ventilated fixed location will not adapt.

If you are willing to keep controlling machinery with your hands (89% almost continuously operating controls) and to judge jams and faults by ear against the sound of the equipment running, this job suits you; people used to reading only screen values and unwilling to confirm at the machine will struggle.

If you are willing to work closely with the crew by shift (70% consider working with the crew extremely important and 58% are in continuous contact with others), to work in cramped and awkward postures (50% every day) and to accept 47% of weeks over 40 hours, this job can be done long term; people who only want to work independently and dislike coordination and handover will not adapt.

If you are willing to stop the machine, withdraw people and then report when you find gas over the limit, poor ventilation or unstable roof support, and to leave inspection and handover records, this occupation is worth learning more about; treating an anomaly as a small problem and continuing to run the machine is usually paid for by the whole crew.

Situations where this is not a good choice: being unwilling to complete methane testing, ventilation and roof support checks before starting the machine, being unwilling to coordinate with signals and the crew, being unable to accept dust and high noise, finding it hard to keep stable control in cramped spaces and under vibration, or tending to keep working after finding an anomaly. Boundary: the exercises and judgments on this page are only for self-checking and do not constitute hiring standards, qualification determinations or underground work authorization; for mine safety training, blasting, electrical and equipment operation authorization, follow the rules of your organization and the competent authorities.

How to try it: for a fictional scenario (in the middle of a night shift at a continuous mining face, the methane reading is close to the limit and new separation signs appear in the roof, while the conveyor jams) write a one-page handling plan, including the stop-and-withdraw sequence, the confirmation actions for ventilation and testing, the basis for judging support reinforcement, who needs to confirm and how it will be documented.

Before starting, confirm: you can break a work cycle into three categories, pre-work checks, machine operation and loading, and equipment maintenance and handover, and explain whether each item is based on procedure requirements, on-site test data or crew instructions; and you can state before deciding which conditions you have verified and which still need testing or confirmation from a supervisor.

Note: this page does not cover roof bolter or mining helper content. Roof bolters specialise in installing bolts and cables to reinforce the roof, and mining helpers handle clearing, carrying and assistance; this occupation's core duty is operating self-propelled mining machines for continuous cutting and loading, and the three have different authorization and outputs.

In one sentence: this is a job whose core is completing pre-work checks to procedure, then operating a continuous mining machine by feel and by ear to cut and load, and stopping, withdrawing people and reporting immediately when methane, ventilation or support is abnormal; it suits people who can keep stable control in high noise, dust and vibration, are willing to work closely with the crew and take on safety responsibility.

This occupation has 15 tasks split into 10Core/5Supplemental, and the first five, ventilation 94, methane 94, roof and rib 93, cutting and loading 89 and positioning 88, are importance, not frequency. Work preparation, cutting and loading operation, and maintenance coordination are overlapping editorial groupings; casing pipe, conveyor cleaning, hydraulic supports, environmental technology and rail support assistance are supplemental, not a fixed per-shift process for all positions.
Ventilation and methane testing records, and roof and rib support check results

Example editorial task chain: check ventilation, gas and support records, position conditions and reporting items under actual qualification authorization; statutory testing and start-of-work confirmation are carried out by the corresponding personnel, and a record on this page cannot approve starting the machine.
Shift work records, and continuous loading and equipment status information

Example editorial operation chain: position, locate and cut and load to the actual equipment plan, monitor status and record doubtful points; starting, moving, personnel positioning and work boundaries are checked separately against the applicable rules.

Observe to the actual equipment procedures and task qualifications, take faulty equipment out of service and hand it over to authorized personnel for repair; supplemental conveyor cleaning or support tasks are not uniformly carried by this occupation. U.S. underground coal mine 75.1725 requires equipment to be safe, hazardous conditions to be taken out of service immediately and only authorized persons to operate it; maintenance requires de-energising and blocking movement, with exceptions for necessary movement during adjustment and for extended fittings during manual lubrication while equipment is running. Not all jurisdictions have a uniform lockout and bleed-off procedure, and repair and restoration duties are checked against the actual equipment rules.

This page compares this occupation with adjacent occupations item by item across seven dimensions: core purpose, main objects and basis, core process, main outputs, responsible party, admission and permits, and conclusion boundary. Extraction occupations all work in mines or quarries, but the objects and authorization of cutting and loading, roof reinforcement, drilling and blasting, haulage and auxiliary work do not transfer just because the workplace is the same; conditions differ markedly between surface and underground and between extraction and equipment services, and when comparing, check the position's actual duties item by item against the seven dimensions in the comparison table on this page.

Core purposes of adjacent occupations: roof bolters specialise in installing bolts and cables to reinforce the roof and ribs, underground haulage machine operators move already cut material to a transfer point, quarry workers split stone to size, blasters drill and blast, and mining helpers carry out clearing and carrying and other auxiliary work.

Operating a self-propelled mining machine for continuous cutting and loading is the occupational definition; ventilation, methane and support tasks are checked against actual qualification and the division of responsibility, and the job title does not guarantee all conditions.

Objects and basis of adjacent occupations: bolts and cables and support design (roof bolters), haulage equipment and transport routes (underground haulage machine operators), stone and splitting tools (quarry workers), explosives and blast design (blasters), and tools and cleared material (mining helpers).

A self-propelled continuous mining machine and its cutting device, ventilation ducting and curtains, methane detectors, and roof and rib support systems; the basis is mine safety procedures, operating procedures and technical briefings, on-site test data and crew instructions.

Processes of adjacent occupations: installing and testing bolts to the design (roof bolters), loading and transferring already cut material (haulage machine operators), splitting and shaping stone to size (quarry workers), drilling, charging and firing (blasters), and clearing, carrying and assisting the trades (mining helpers).

Preparation checks, equipment positioning and cutting and loading, and maintenance handover are overlapping editorial processes, and a fixed arrow chart cannot replace mine operating procedures and the responsibilities for checks and release.

Outputs of adjacent occupations: support installation and testing records (roof bolters), haulage volume and transport records (haulage machine operators), stone specification and output (quarry workers), blast design and firing records (blasters), and clearing and material handling results (mining helpers).

The amount of material cut and loaded during the shift, ventilation and methane testing records, roof and rib support check results, equipment status and repair and replacement records, and shift handover records.

Responsible parties of adjacent occupations: roof bolters are responsible for the quality of support installation, haulage machine operators for haulage work and transport safety, quarry workers for stone specification, blasters for blasting work and guarding, and mining helpers for the auxiliary work they carry out.

China's Coal Mine Safety Regulations No. 17 take effect on 2026-02-01; Article 9 requires safety education and training to be passed before going on shift, and special operations additionally require training and qualification under national rules; the 2026-06-01 special operations catalogue lists 5.7 coal shearers, 5.8 roadheaders and 5.4 gas inspection separately, checked against the actual equipment task, and they do not automatically transfer to each other; coal-mine certificate requirements are not automatically applied to all metal and non-metal mine operators. Article 8 of the Chinese coal mine regulations provides that a person has the right to stop work immediately and withdraw to a safe place when there is a dangerous situation at the workplace, and may refuse work when the danger remains unresolved and personal safety cannot be ensured; permission does not have to be waited for in order to avoid danger. Article 126 requires the shift leader to inspect the work face comprehensively before work starts and only then may personnel enter, and general operator experience does not replace that duty. U.S. underground coal mine 30 CFR 75.362: the shift inspection is carried out by a certified person designated by the operator, and methane testing is carried out by a qualified person before power is applied and at other points and at required intervals during operation; the dust control inspection includes ventilation and spray parameters and the plan. Certificate status and general operators are checked separately, and sensors or screens do not automatically remove the required testing.

This page does not provide preparation levels or qualification requirements for adjacent occupations; these must be checked item by item against each occupation's official pages, the employer's safety training system and the competent authority's rules.

Current O*NET education respondent proportions are high school or equivalent 81%, postsecondary certificate 10% and some college no degree 5%, only a partial distribution; Zone1—2/SVP below 6 with training from a few days to a year is a general description of the preparation grouping, not a uniform duration for this position. BLS table 1.2 for this occupation typically shows no formal educational credential, no related occupational experience and medium-term OJT, and typical statistics do not exempt actual employer and mine training and task qualification. U.S. 30 CFR 48.5 applies to new underground miners: it requires at least 40 hours of training before starting work (about 8 hours at the mine), with exceptions for rehired already trained persons checked separately; this differs from the general Zone description and from the position's medium-term OJT. Surface, new-task and other personnel conditions were not checked item by item.

Similar extraction workplaces do not mean roles are interchangeable: whether you carry responsibility for cutting and loading, roof reinforcement, drilling and blasting, haulage or auxiliary work determines the scope of authorization and where responsibility lies.

Six recurring professional judgments: whether ventilation and methane conditions are met; whether roof and rib support is stable; whether the cutting position and depth are set to the operating procedure; whether equipment jams and faults are handled promptly; whether signals and coordination with the crew are clear; and whether anomalies are handled by stopping, withdrawing people and reporting to procedure.
Judgment one: are ventilation and methane conditions met?

U.S. underground coal mine 30 CFR 75.362: the shift inspection is carried out by a certified person designated by the operator, and methane testing is carried out by a qualified person before power is applied and at other points and at required intervals during operation; the dust control inspection includes ventilation and spray parameters and the plan. Certificate status and general operators are checked separately, and sensors or screens do not automatically remove the required testing. U.S. underground coal mine 75.323 sets different requirements for equipment de-energisation, ventilation adjustment, work restrictions in affected areas and withdrawal of personnel at 1.0% and 1.5% methane at the workplace and in the intake air stream, with return air cases separated out; approaching the limit or any anomaly cannot be given the same withdrawal and restart steps, still less transferred to Chinese thresholds.
Judgment two: is roof and rib support stable?

Article 133 of the Chinese coal mine regulations requires continuous miner mining to have a mining design and stoping procedure and full-pressure ventilation, prohibits work under unsupported roof and requires reinforcement at connecting exits, sets the cutting depth according to the roof, equipment and process, and requires ventilation curtains to be adjusted promptly; there are prohibition conditions for outburst mines, high-gas mines in specified circumstances, seams with a dip greater than 8° or unstable immediate roofs. The applicable conditions are checked against the full text and the actual mine, and this page does not approve mining. U.S. underground coal mine 75.202 requires the roof and ribs of work and travel areas to be supported or controlled, and that subpart restricts work and travel under unsupported roof; supplemental casing pipe tasks are not treated as the support method for all mines or as the operator's design authority.
Judgment three: are the cutting position and depth determined?
Determine the cutting position, boundaries and depth to the operating procedure, avoiding off-line cutting, over-excavation or damage to supports and equipment.
Judgment four: has the equipment anomaly been handled?

U.S. underground coal mine 75.1725 requires equipment to be safe, hazardous conditions to be taken out of service immediately and only authorized persons to operate it; maintenance requires de-energising and blocking movement, with exceptions for necessary movement during adjustment and for extended fittings during manual lubrication while equipment is running. Not all jurisdictions have a uniform lockout and bleed-off procedure, and repair and restoration duties are checked against the actual equipment rules. This round did not obtain evidence that a fault necessarily leads to a major overhaul.
Judgment five: are crew coordination and signals clear?

Article 142 of the coal mine regulations applies to tunneling with roadheaders, bolter miners, continuous miners and similar equipment: before starting, check that no one is in front of the apron or near the cutting arm and that the remote operator is in a safe position, and give a warning; it requires spray or linkage for dust reduction, prohibits crossing under the arm while running and standing between the machine body and the coal or rock wall; when stopping and at shift handover the cutting head must be lowered to the ground and the power cut. Specific equipment and working methods are checked separately and are not applied to all coal and metal and non-metal processes.
Judgment six: have the abnormal stop and reporting been done?

Article 8 of the Chinese coal mine regulations provides that a person has the right to stop work immediately and withdraw to a safe place when there is a dangerous situation at the workplace, and may refuse work when the danger remains unresolved and personal safety cannot be ensured; permission does not have to be waited for in order to avoid danger. Article 126 requires the shift leader to inspect the work face comprehensively before work starts and only then may personnel enter, and general operator experience does not replace that duty. Methane, ventilation, support and equipment situations are handled under their respective real systems, and reporting, rectification and restarting are checked separately and are not uniformly equated with a single operating permit.

Continuous mining machine operators drive self-propelled mining machines to cut coal, metal and non-metal ore, rock and sand and gravel continuously at the ore body face and load the material onto conveyors, shuttle cars or trucks; before work they check ventilation and methane and confirm that roof and rib support is stable, during work they monitor equipment operation, and after work they maintain machine parts and change cutting teeth. The entry name on this page follows the frozen index as machine operator and corresponds to the official occupation Continuous Mining Machine Operators (O*NET-SOC 47-5041.00).

Positioning | Determine the cutting position and depth | Drive the machine into position at the work face, determine the position, boundaries and depth of the hole or cutting channel, and reposition as needed to complete additional drilling or cutting.
Control | Control the conveying and cutting devices | Operate controls to start and adjust conveyor operation, start and position the drill or cutting head, and make cutting and loading continuous.

Safety | Check ventilation, methane and roof and ribs under qualification duties | The first three tasks are Core and casing pipe is Supplemental; professional testing, crew start-of-work checks and support design are not uniformly carried by general operators.

Maintenance | Observe and repair under actual equipment authorization | Observation by ear and maintenance are Core; taking out of service, de-energising and blocking movement follow the specific equipment rules, and the occupational tasks do not automatically confer electromechanical repair qualification.

Coordination | Conveyor cleaning and rail support are supplemental | Carried out to the specific project task and qualification, and cannot be treated as the core for all positions or as general support authority for all positions.

Communication | face-to-face 84%/16%, every day and every week, contact with others 58%/35%, continuously and most of the time; telephone 29%/66%, every day and never, so no share of spoken commands and signals is inferred. Schedule | 90% fixed arrangement, work week 47%/53%, over 40 and forty; deadlines 30%/27%, every day and every week, not repair continuation intensity. Team | 70%/22%, extremely important and very; decision freedom 36%/34%/26%, a lot, some and limited, with task priority a separate question, and actual reporting follows the mine. Evidence note: the occupational scope and adjacent relationships in this table are based on O*NET related occupations and the 2018 SOC classification; tasks and work context are based on the O*NET 47-5041.00 occupation details; U.S. wages and employment are based on the exact occupation scope of the O*NET national wages page and summary page (2025 wage data, 2024 employment and 2024—2034 projections), together with the 2025—2035 scope of the BLS employment projections table (no separate row figure for this occupation was obtained in this round). Adjacent relationships do not mean qualifications transfer, that positions are interchangeable, or that underground work authorization or safety training evidence can be transferred.

The table below places this occupation and five adjacent occupations on the same set of dimensions: for each direction it first states the core work and outputs, then the key differences from this occupation, and finally when that direction is a better choice.

Roof bolters specialise in installing and testing support components, with authorization concentrated on the support work itself; this occupation operates the mining machine for continuous cutting and loading after checking support conditions and does not carry the conclusions of support component installation and testing.

If you would rather focus on roof reinforcement and support quality, look at the roof bolters direction; if you would rather operate equipment for continuous cutting and loading, look at this occupation.
Install bolts and cables to the support design at the extraction face to reinforce the roof and ribs, test installation quality, and produce support installation and testing records.
Roof Bolters, Mining

Underground haulage machine operators deal with hauling and transferring already cut material, starting after the material is heaped; this occupation cuts the material from the work face and loads it continuously, upstream of the haulage step.

If you would rather focus on haulage equipment and transport organisation, look at the underground haulage machine operators direction; if you would rather cut and load directly at the work face, look at this occupation.
Operate underground haulage equipment to move already cut material to a transfer point or transport system, producing haulage volume and transport records.
Loading and Moving Machine Operators, Underground Mining

Quarry workers aim at stone specification and output and work mainly by splitting and shaping; this occupation deals with continuous cutting and loading of coal, metal and non-metal ore bodies and is constrained by underground ventilation, methane and roof conditions.

If you would rather split and shape stone in a surface quarry, look at the quarry workers direction; if you would rather operate continuous mining equipment under controlled safety conditions, look at this occupation.
Split and shape stone blocks to size in a surface quarry, producing stone that meets specification.
Rock Splitters, Quarry

Excavating and loading machine and dragline operators work on the surface, mainly with excavating and loading equipment, and are not constrained by underground ventilation and methane conditions; this occupation works continuously underground or in underground extraction areas, has more safety check steps and concentrates responsibility on confirming work face conditions.

If you would rather operate excavating and loading equipment in a surface quarry, look at that direction; if you would rather operate a continuous mining machine in an underground extraction area, look at this occupation.
Operate excavators, loaders or draglines to strip and load material in a surface mine, producing stripping volume and loading records.
Excavating and Loading Machine and Dragline Operators, Surface Mining

Blasters are responsible for blast design and firing safety, and the work involves a single strong destructive event and strict guarding requirements; this occupation works by continuous, controllable mechanical cutting and does not carry responsibility for charging and firing.

If you would rather do drilling, blasting and guarding organisation, look at the blasters direction; if you would rather advance the work face continuously by mechanical means, look at this occupation.
Drill, charge and fire to the blast design, take responsibility for guarding and firing safety, and produce blast design and firing records.
Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters

Mining helpers carry out auxiliary work as arranged on site, with authorization and responsibility limited to the auxiliary processes they take on; this occupation is responsible for the shift's continuous cutting and loading work itself and for checking the safety conditions before work.

If you would rather start by learning about an extraction site through clearing and carrying and other auxiliary work, look at the mining helpers direction; if you would rather operate the core equipment directly, look at this occupation.
Carry out clearing, carrying, material transfer and assistance at the extraction site, producing clearing and material handling results.
Mining helpers

If you are torn between two directions, first run a small experiment with a fictional shift status pack: write a one-page status statement (the shift's work face conditions, equipment status, the loading volume to be completed and who needs to confirm), then see whether you would rather be responsible for continuous cutting and loading, for roof support, for haulage, for drilling and blasting, or for auxiliary work.

paragraphs: Job seekers preparing to enter and career changers

First master the basic requirements of mine safety procedures (ventilation, methane, roof and rib support, dust and noise protection), the structure and operating procedures of the equipment, and how to judge the cutting position and depth, then build experience through positions with safety training and crew leading; do not skip the safety training step and go straight onto the machine.
Operators already working at extraction sites

Use equipment monitoring and data recording tools for status trend viewing and handover records, but ventilation, methane and support checks before starting the machine and the judgment to stop and withdraw people when something is abnormal must still be confirmed on site to procedure; do not let screen readings replace on-site checks.
Managers responsible for extraction area safety and production

Article 8 of the Chinese coal mine regulations provides that a person has the right to stop work immediately and withdraw to a safe place when there is a dangerous situation at the workplace, and may refuse work when the danger has not been handled in a way that cannot ensure personal safety; permission does not have to be waited for in order to avoid danger. Article 126 requires the shift leader to inspect the work face comprehensively before work starts and only then may personnel enter, and general operator experience does not replace that duty. Statutory testing, repair and restoration are carried out by personnel who actually hold the qualification, and emergency avoidance cannot be written as requiring a wait for permission.
People planning to move into support, haulage or electromechanical repair

Fill in the definitions and methods of the corresponding position (support design and installation testing, haulage equipment and transport organisation, equipment repair and fault diagnosis) and demonstrate readiness with verifiable outputs (support installation and testing records, haulage records, repair records).

values: Fictional shift materials (exercise input)

Fictional scenario: in the middle of a night shift at an underground continuous coal mining face, the methane reading is close to the limit and new separation signs appear in the roof, while the conveyor jams, and the crew leader asks for coal output to resume as soon as possible.

Materials provided: excerpts of the operating procedure's ventilation, methane and support check requirements; the ventilation and methane testing records for the first two hours of the shift; the roof and rib support inspection record; a preliminary description of the conveyor jam; the shift's output target.

Materials not provided: the instrument's historical data on the methane reading trend, the measured extent of the separation, the specific mechanical cause of the jam, and the output adjustment the supervisor would accept. If these conditions are needed in the exercise, state your assumptions and who you need to confirm them with.
Task requirements

Write a one-page handling plan: including the judgment and sequence for stopping the machine and withdrawing people, the confirmation actions for ventilation and methane testing, the recommendation for roof and rib support, the handling of the equipment jam and repair arrangements, and the parties to communicate the output adjustment to and how it will be documented.
The plan must state which conditions you have verified and which are still assumptions, and explain whether it relies on the operating procedure, testing records or on-site observation.
Reference deliverable (derivable from the prompt)

The plan should include: current status judgment (the relationship of the methane reading to the limit, the position and extent of the separation signs, the effect of the jam on the conveying step), handling sequence (stop the machine and withdraw people and strengthen ventilation first, then verify gas and support conditions, and handle the jam once conditions allow), repair arrangements (handled under the shutdown and lockout procedure with the responsible person confirmed), communication and documentation (reporting to the shift supervisor, coordinating with the transport position, recording the handling process) and risk notes (unclear reading trend and uncertain extent of the separation).
The reference deliverable lists only the elements that should be included and does not require the same wording as the example; being able to explain the basis for your judgment is enough.
Boundaries and conclusions that cannot be inferred

This exercise only tests safety procedure awareness, the approach to handling equipment anomalies and document organisation ability; it does not assess the safety conditions or compliance of a real mine, and does not constitute hiring, a qualification judgment or handling advice for real work.
Do not use testing records, repair or incident material from real mines; for real work, follow the rules of your organization and the competent authorities.
Deliverable one: pre-start checklist and testing record
Deliverable: a fictional shift checklist, including confirmation of ventilation facilities, methane testing readings and support inspection results.
The checklist must state which clause of the operating procedure each item relies on, and the handling action when the conditions are not met.
Deliverable two: equipment anomaly judgment and shutdown statement
Deliverable: a one-page statement recording the abnormal phenomena, the basis for the judgment, the shutdown and reporting sequence and the conditions for resuming work.
The statement must distinguish phenomena observed on site from suspected causes, and must not present a suspicion as a conclusion.
Deliverable three: shift handover record
Deliverable: a handover record stating the work face conditions, equipment status, completed and outstanding items, and the safety conditions the next shift must watch.
Tool statement

Deliverable: a one-page statement listing the testing record sheets, equipment status recording methods and document archiving methods you have used and their purposes; real mine testing and incident material must not be included.

values: Day 1: read a public mine safety requirement
Find a public mine safety procedure or operating requirement material, mark three requirements related to ventilation, methane testing and roof support, and write down the points you want to confirm.
Day 2: prepare a pre-start checklist
Using a fictional shift, organise ventilation facility confirmation, gas testing and support checking into an executable checklist, and note the action when conditions are not met.
Day 3: read and interpret data once
Using fictional testing records, judge the relationship between the reading trend and the limit, and write how you would handle it with the basis explained.
Day 4: write an equipment anomaly judgment
Using fictional abnormal noise and jam symptoms, write the possible causes, the shutdown sequence and the conditions to confirm before resuming work.
Day 5: write a handover record
Write a shift handover record including work face conditions, equipment status and the safety matters the next shift must watch.
Day 6: write the abnormal shutdown and reporting sequence
Write the complete sequence when gas exceeds the limit, ventilation is interrupted or support is abnormal (stop work, withdraw people, report, confirm, resume), and note who needs to confirm.
Day 7: decide whether to continue
Go back to the judgment checklist on this page and write down three reasons you are willing to continue and two conditions that call for caution.

Exercise cost: reading procedures and testing data, operating continuously in noise and dust, and shift handover and records, which step drains you most, and can you accept it recurring every shift.
Material boundary: the exercise materials are all fictional or based on public materials, and real mine testing, repair and incident material must not be included.
Response to feedback: when your plan is pointed out to be missing ventilation or support conditions, are you willing to go back to the procedure and testing basis and fill the gaps.
Process interest: even when the process repeats, are you willing to complete the checks, testing and handover records every shift.

Next step: if you are willing to continue with the first six steps, the next step is to complete a loop from pre-start checks to shift handover under compliant conditions (such as a training course, simulated equipment or de-identified materials) and have an experienced crew leader review it; if a step clearly drains you, narrow the direction first and verify again.

entries.limitation: Article 9 requires safety education and training to be passed before going on shift, and special operations require separate training and qualification under national rules. Article 8 of the Chinese coal mine regulations provides that a person has the right to stop work immediately and withdraw to a safe place when there is a dangerous situation at the workplace, and may refuse work when the danger has not been handled in a way that cannot ensure personal safety, so permission does not have to be waited for in order to avoid danger. Article 126 requires the shift leader to inspect the work face comprehensively before work starts and only then may personnel enter, and general operator experience does not replace that duty. Article 133 requires continuous miner mining to have a mining design and stoping procedure and full-pressure ventilation, prohibits work under unsupported roof and requires reinforcement at connecting exits, sets the cutting depth according to the roof, equipment and process, and requires ventilation curtains to be adjusted promptly; there are prohibition conditions for outburst mines, high-gas mines in specified circumstances, seams with a dip greater than 8° or unstable immediate roofs. The applicable conditions are checked against the full text and the actual mine, and this page does not approve mining. Article 142 of the coal mine regulations covers roadheaders, bolter miners, continuous miners and similar equipment: before starting, check that no one is in front of the apron or near the cutting arm and that the remote operator is in a safe position, and give a warning; it requires spray or linkage for dust reduction, prohibits crossing under the arm while running and standing between the machine body and the coal or rock wall; when stopping and at shift handover the cutting head must be lowered to the ground and the power cut. Specific equipment and working methods are checked separately and are not applied to all coal and metal and non-metal processes.

subject.name: Continuous mining machine operator
subject.summary: Continuous mining machine operators drive self-propelled mining machines to cut coal, metal and non-metal ore, rock and sand and gravel continuously at the ore body face and load the material onto conveyors, shuttle cars or trucks; before work they check ventilation and methane and confirm that roof and rib support is stable, during work they monitor equipment operation, and after work they maintain machine parts and change cutting teeth.
